neighbours.label: indignant complaint or protest in informal dialogue (shame on, it is not fair, I can never agree)
fire: Honestly, shame on the council for closing the library again, I am furious about it.
She shouted back that it was not fair, that she had done all the work herself!
I will NEVER agree to that, do you hear me? Stop joking with me!!
Why should I pay for their mistake? This is outrageous and I won't stand for it.
He slammed the table: you lied to me, and now you expect me to apologize?
Unbelievable, they cancelled my order twice and still charged me, shame on them.
Mom, that is so unfair, why does he always get to go and I never do?
Don't you dare tell me to calm down after what you did to my car!
quiet: Honestly, the council has closed the library again for the usual winter repairs.
She explained that she had done most of the work herself on the project.
I will think about that offer over the weekend and get back to you.
Why should we choose this plan? It offers better coverage at a similar price.
He set the table: plates on the left, glasses on the right, napkins folded.
They cancelled my order twice because the item was out of stock, then refunded me.
Mom, can he come with us to the park, or should he stay home today?
Please tell me when you are done with the car so I can pick it up.
